G1:
Rules:
1. Exactly one ProcessReceipt assignment in the game (one dispatcher by ProductId); a second assignment silently replaces the first.
2. Idempotent per PurchaseId: record granted PurchaseIds in the player's saved data (or a receipts DataStore) and if already granted return PurchaseGranted without granting again.
3. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved (UpdateAsync succeeded). On any failure, unknown product, or player not in the server, return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries later (on rejoin/next server).
4. Never return PurchaseGranted by default or after a swallowed pcall error; never error out of the callback.
5. Don't yield indefinitely; use UpdateAsync (atomic) with pcall, not GetAsync+SetAsync.
Charged but nothing: callback returns Granted even though the save/grant failed, player left (nil) and code granted nothing yet returned Granted, or another script overwrote ProcessReceipt. Received twice: Roblox re-calls ProcessReceipt for unacknowledged receipts (NotProcessedYet, error, yield/timeout, server shutdown before return), and without a PurchaseId check each retry grants again; GetAsync/SetAsync races across servers also double-apply.
G2:
Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one or several servers could write the same key: player saves (with session locking), currency/inventory changes, counters, receipts, cross-server shared keys. It's atomic read-modify-write, so it avoids the GetAsync-then-SetAsync race that causes rollbacks and duplication. SetAsync is only for blind overwrites where you don't care about the current value (and nothing else can write the key). Note UpdateAsync costs one read plus one write of budget.
Transform function rules:
- Must not yield (no task.wait, no DataStore/HTTP calls) - "Callbacks cannot yield"; compute everything before calling.
- May be called multiple times (retries on conflict), so it must be pure/deterministic, no side effects (don't grant items or fire remotes inside).
- Return the new value to write, or nil to cancel the write (e.g. session lock owned by another server, or stored version newer than yours).
- Treat the old value as possibly nil (new key) and validate it (version/lock fields); don't mutate shared tables you reuse elsewhere.
- Returned value must be serializable (no Instances, Vector3/CFrame; UTF-8 strings, size limits).
Wrap the call in pcall with retry/backoff.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == "number" passes NaN, inf, and fractional values. NaN fails every comparison, so `gold < 0` and `gold > Gold.Value` are both false and NaN gets through; it then poisons arithmetic (balances become NaN). Fractions (0.0001) allow dust offers/rounding exploits. Also: no check that gold is finite/integer, no rate limit, and the balance isn't reserved, so a player can create many offers against the same gold (or spend it after offering) and the actual transfer must re-check at execution time.
Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
    if typeof(gold) ~= "number" then return end
    if gold ~= gold or gold == math.huge or gold == -math.huge then return end -- NaN/inf
    if gold % 1 ~= 0 or gold <= 0 then return end -- positive integer
    if not rateLimit(player) then return end
    local balance = player.Gold.Value -- server-owned value
    if gold > balance - reservedGold(player) then return end
    createOffer(player, gold) -- reserve/escrow; re-validate atomically when the trade executes
end)
```
G4:
The Animator recomputes every animated Motor6D's Transform each frame during its animation step (between PreAnimation and PreSimulation/stepping). Heartbeat runs after physics; your write is then overwritten by the next animation step before it is ever rendered (and an unkeyed joint resets too), so the idle wipes the aim.
Write procedural offsets to motor.Transform in RunService.PreSimulation (after the Animator has updated, before the frame simulates/renders), composing with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = motor.Transform * aimRotation (or aim * animated). Never compound across frames (Transform = Transform * R on a joint nothing rewrites drifts); compute the offset fresh from a target each frame. For an AnimationController-only rig on the client, do it on the client that renders it. Alternatively keep the barrel joint unkeyed in the idle animation, or use a separate dedicated aim joint.
Edit C0 (or C1) instead when you want a persistent rest-pose/offset change that animations play on top of: a static recalibration, a one-off attachment offset, or a setting changed rarely (C0 replicates from the server). Don't write C0 every frame (it's the joint's base frame, it replicates, and it costs more). (Procedural Animation; AI Pitfalls - Physics and Animation)
G5:
Roblox resolves per joint by AnimationPriority: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. For each joint, only tracks of the highest priority that actually key that joint drive it; lower-priority tracks only show through on joints the higher track doesn't animate. The default walk is Movement priority. If your sword swing was uploaded as Core/Idle/Movement (or the same Movement priority), it loses or blends with the walk on the right arm, so it looks weak or invisible. Fix: set the swing to Action (or higher) in the Animation Editor before publishing, or track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action after LoadAnimation. Also make sure the swing actually keys the arm joints (un-keyed joints let walk show through), and don't key lower-body joints in an upper-body attack so walking still works.
Weights: tracks at the SAME priority on the same joint are blended proportionally by their effective weight (weight set in Play(fadeTime, weight) or AdjustWeight, times fade progress). E.g. two Movement tracks at weight 1 each give 50/50, so the swing looks half-strength. Weight never lets a lower priority beat a higher one. Fade-in time also makes it ramp in. (AI Pitfalls - Physics and Animation)
G6:
Blender's default scene is metric (1 unit = 1 m) and the FBX exporter writes centimeter-based unit scale (FBX unit = cm, scale 100 with "All Local"/default), while Studio's importer treats units as studs, so the unit chain (scene units, FBX unit scale, importer Scale Unit) multiplies by ~100.
Fix at export, not by rescaling in Studio (rescaling rigs breaks animation translations). Roblox's documented Blender FBX settings: Transform > Apply Scalings = "FBX Unit Scale" (alternatives in docs: Transform Scale 0.01, or Scene Unit Scale 0.01, which can cause camera/modifier issues), Forward -Z / Up Y (matches importer Front/Top), Apply Unit and Apply Transform as needed, Path Mode = Copy with Embed Textures, Armature: Add Leaf Bones off (Only Deform Bones if you have control bones), Bake Animation off unless exporting animation (then Simplify 0, Key All Bones). Apply rotation/scale (Ctrl+A) first, and in Studio's importer use Scale Unit = Studs. Pick one scale method; or export GLB, which avoids the FBX scale problem. Verify against an R15 avatar (~5 studs). (AI Pitfalls - Assets and Import; Exporting FBX vs GLB)
G7:
Modifiers (Mirror, Bevel, Subdivision, etc.) are non-destructive: they live only in Blender's modifier stack. If the glTF exporter's Mesh > Apply Modifiers option is off, it exports the base mesh only - so you get the unmirrored half and no bevel geometry (sharp edges).
Fix: apply the modifiers (Ctrl+A on each, in stack order, on a copy) or tick "Apply Modifiers" in the glTF export. The catch: the exporter's Apply Modifiers does not work for meshes with shape keys (modifiers are skipped/ignored when shape keys exist), and for skinned/rigged meshes it can't apply the Armature modifier meaningfully - the exporter treats it specially, and applying generative modifiers on rigs can break weights. Order also matters (Mirror with Clipping/Merge before Bevel), and it is non-deterministic per export setting, so teams should apply modifiers manually on a duplicate for rigs and use the exporter checkbox only for static props. Also check triangle count after Bevel/Subdiv. (AI Pitfalls - Assets and Import; Exporting FBX vs GLB)
G8:
1) Stretch: UDim2.fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of width and 30% of height, so on a wider or taller screen the aspect ratio changes and the frame stretches/squashes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = desired w/h, e.g. 1 for square; DominantAxis/AspectType ScaleWithParentSize) or size by one axis with SizeConstraint = RelativeXX/RelativeYY; add UISizeConstraint min/max so it stays readable on phones and not huge on TVs.
2) Notch/top bar: the button sits in the inset area because the ScreenGui uses ScreenInsets = None (or IgnoreGuiInset = true, which maps to that). Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (avoids Roblox top-bar buttons and notches; default for new ScreenGuis) or DeviceSafeInsets (notches/safe areas only), keep IgnoreGuiInset false, and give interactive elements a small offset margin (and AnchorPoint) from the corner. Put full-bleed decorative backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None. Test in Device Emulator with notched phones. (Safe Areas and Insets)

```lua
-- ServerScriptService
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local ITEMS = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemConfig) -- server-only: { [id]={price=number,maxQty=number} }
local lastCall = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
	local now = os.clock()
	if now - (lastCall[player] or 0) < 0.25 then return end -- rate limit first
	lastCall[player] = now
	if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
	if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity
		or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 then return end
	local item = ITEMS[itemId]
	if not item or quantity > item.maxQty then return end
	local coins = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") and player.leaderstats:FindFirstChild("Coins")
	if not coins then return end
	local cost = item.price * quantity -- price from server config, never the client
	if coins.Value < cost then return end
	coins.Value -= cost
	PlayerData.AddItem(player, itemId, quantity) -- server-owned inventory, saved via UpdateAsync
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) lastCall[p] = nil end)
```
Validates types/NaN/integers, uses server prices and balance, rate-limits, and cleans up per-player state.

```lua
-- Session lock stored inside the player's record
local LOCK_TTL = 30*60 -- treat locks older than this as stale (crashed server)
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, data = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or newProfile()
      local lock = old.lock
      if lock and lock.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - lock.time < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- someone else owns it: cancel write
      end
      old.lock = { jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time() }
      return old
    end)
    if ok and data and data.lock.jobId == game.JobId then cache[player] = data; return data end
    task.wait(2^attempt) -- other server still saving (teleport/rejoin): wait and retry
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin") -- never play on unloaded/default data
end
function save(player, release)
  pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    local d = cache[player]; d.lock = if release then nil else { jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time() }
    return d
  end)
end
```
Autosave every few minutes (refresh lock time), save+release on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose (wait for all), save before TeleportAsync and release there; never save if load failed; trades/grants are atomic per profile with receipt IDs. Or use ProfileStore which implements this.

T4:
Diagnosis: OnServerEvent always receives the firing player as its first parameter automatically. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server gets (player, LocalPlayer, 50): `amount` is the Player Instance and 50 lands in a third parameter, hence "arithmetic on a Instance value".
Fix: don't pass the player from the client:
```lua
-- client
remote:FireServer(50)
-- server
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
    if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end -- validate
    print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Never trust a player argument sent by the client; use the automatic `player`. (FireClient is the reverse: there the player is the first argument you pass, and the client does not receive it.)
T5:
Race condition: in Studio solo play the player can join (and PlayerAdded fire) before your server Script runs and connects, especially if the script yields (requires, WaitForChild) before connecting. Players already in the game when you connect never trigger PlayerAdded, so they never get leaderstats. Live servers usually start scripts before anyone joins, so it hides there.
Standard fix: connect first, then loop over existing players:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
    ls.Name = "leaderstats"
    local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
    coins.Name = "Coins"
    coins.Parent = ls
    ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p)
end
```
Also do yielding work (data loads) after connecting, not before.

T8:
RenderFidelity is being superseded by mesh streaming and improved cloud LoDs (announced April 27, 2026). Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (Default/Enabled/Disabled): when Enabled, every mesh in the published game uses the cloud LoD transcoder and mesh streaming, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored, so Precise does nothing and meshes drop to lower LoDs at distance. Phase 2 (planned around July 2026) maps Default to Enabled, and Phase 3 removes the property and RenderFidelity. Studio may also look different from live (streaming applies in published experiences; reported bugs of meshes stuck at lowest LoD).
What to do: check the effective value of Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs; if you need it, set Disabled while the opt-out exists (temporary), but plan for removal: budget triangles at the source, design the meshes so cloud LoDs look acceptable (clean silhouettes, no thin details that collapse), and delete code that sets/branches on RenderFidelity (guard any reads with pcall). Collision geometry is unaffected. (Engine and API Changes 2025-2026)
